change_summary: Owner authorized and executed roadmap Phase 1 of the AI assistant (D-36 literal scope): deterministic analytics, two read-only built-in tools, shared-core Algerian dialect synonyms, and synthetic-data tests.

Added deterministic analytics in BuiltInAssistant: average sale value, day/week comparison, overdue debts and period totals, all computed from the existing store snapshot with no free-form SQL and no numbers generated from text; added previous-week fields to the snapshot.

Added two read-only tools to BuiltInToolRegistry (EmbeddedAnalyticsTool, ProductLookupTool) that read the same snapshot and never write to the database; kept answer intent 'أدوات' so number questions stay protected from model replacement.
Added DialectSynonyms.cs for shared-core Algerian Arabic conversation synonyms, stored in normalized form and used in intent matching; no regional dictionaries added.

Verification: build 0 errors; tests 313/313 (24 domain + 289 integration) with synthetic data only; all final numbers still come from embedded deterministic queries, three-path routing and manual choice unchanged, nothing sent to the cloud and no cloud keys enabled.

Owner approved and integrated the next-generation AI assistant architecture (D-36): cooperation between the built-in, local and cloud paths, with the built-in as the permanent guard for all final numbers.

Ten binding constants recorded in PROJECT_RULES.md section 9.1 (version 0.3.1): three paths retained, protected number questions, mandatory question redaction before cloud sharing, separate cloud-model and cloud-sharing toggles, three work modes with built-in adjudication, and the approved privacy wording.

Language priority approved: Arabic first, Algerian dialect as a separate conversation-only support layer (shared core now, regional dictionaries later), French as passive support now with professional parity deferred to a later version.

Added docs/proposals/AI_ORCHESTRATION_ARCHITECTURE_PROPOSED_AR.md as an approved active reference; this is a documentation and architecture decision only and grants no implementation authorization for roadmap phases 1 to 6.
Phase 3 full implementation authorized by the owner (D-34): cash drawer and cash counting with opening float, cash movements, and shift close with a counted-cash difference.
Added the SHR purchase document with purchase cost stored per line, a purchases page with item lists and a purchases table.
Added the cash dashboard at /cash and cash/purchases report tabs at /reports; purchase costs are hidden from users without ViewPurchaseCosts.
Added four permissions (OperateCashDrawer, ManageCashDrawer, ManagePurchases, ViewPurchaseCosts) with audit entries; cashier navigation and page access are gated accordingly.
Cash drawer is optional: when disabled, shift close falls back to the Phase 2 behaviour; the /cash UI always passes counted cash.
Added four new UI labels/fields in /settings for enabling the drawer and setting the cash-difference tolerance; quick settings stays presentation/preferences only.
Added an additive migration (AddCashDrawerAndPurchases) and 12 integration tests (T-15 to T-25).
Pre-Phase-3 backups lack the CashMovements table and are rejected on restore, as required by BackupService.RequiredTables.
Excluded from scope: sync, cloud, phone/multi-device, supplier ledger, debt collection, cash refund for MRB, inventory valuation/profit, and editing documents after creation.
review_findings: v0.6.16 records the executed roadmap Phase 1 embedded-assistant strengthening. v0.6.15 was a documentation-only integration; no version claims code built, tested, deployed or verified unless stated here.
Build: dotnet build Wizz.sln -c Release --no-restore -v minimal = 0 errors (pre-existing StyleCop warnings only).

Tests: dotnet test Wizz.sln -c Release --no-restore = Domain 24/24; Integration 289/289 (313 total), up from a 274-integration baseline; includes migration, backup/restore and the new synthetic-data Phase 1 tests.
Phase 1 verification used synthetic data only; no real merchant database was queried for these tests and no real-device restore is claimed.
Number guard preserved: tool answers carry the 'أدوات' intent so IsPrecisionAnswer stays true and analytical/local/cloud routing cannot replace embedded numbers.
No external transmission: nothing was sent to any cloud service and no cloud-model or cloud-sharing toggle was enabled.
Roadmap phases 2 to 6 remain unauthorized; professional French (phase 6) is deferred. General execution authorization stays NOT AUTHORIZED except the documented limited scopes.
Browser verification on a synthetic-only SQLite database at localhost:5183: /cash, /purchases, /reports (cash and purchases tabs) and /settings render with no console errors.
Permission check: a cashier sees only the home, sales, debts, cash, stock and AI navigation links; /purchases, /reports and /settings redirect to /access-denied, while /cash stays accessible.
Cost hiding verified in code through CurrentUser.HasPermissionAsync(ViewPurchaseCosts) in the purchases page and the purchases report tab.
Close behaviour verified in code: counting runs only when store.CashDrawerEnabled and a counted cash value is supplied; otherwise the legacy shift.Close() path is used.
Backup limitation: backups taken before Phase 3 have no CashMovements table and are rejected after upgrade; no claim of restorability is made.
CI remains unavailable for the GitHub account (billing issue; owner declined support contact); verification is local and manual.
A real restore in a separate environment (MVP-AT-09) has not been performed.
